scenarios.title: Single weak signal must not cascade into multiple finding types
scenarios.description: Page contains one generic session cookie and a mention of 'consul' in consulting context. A single weak signal must not cascade into technology detection + shadow IT + admin panel + CVE findings.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A single word in body text is not sufficient evidence to identify a running technology. Downstream modules must not treat an unconfirmed technology name as proof.

scenarios.title: Word 'grafana' in article prose is not Grafana software
scenarios.description: Blog article discusses Grafana monitoring in prose text. No Grafana-specific headers, cookies, or structural markers.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A bare substring match on 'grafana' in body text is weak evidence. Without corroborating signals (x-grafana-version header, /api/health endpoint, grafana_session cookie), this should not be classified as Grafana.

scenarios.title: Article about Grafana is not Grafana running
scenarios.description: About page with multiple mentions of 'grafana' in editorial content.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Multiple mentions of a product name in editorial prose do not confirm the product is running on this host.

scenarios.title: Person named 'Hudson' is not Jenkins/Hudson CI
scenarios.description: Team page with employee named Hudson Martinez. The word 'Hudson' is a person's name, not Jenkins/Hudson CI software.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Hudson is a common surname and place name. Body text containing 'Hudson' as a name must not map to Jenkins CI.

scenarios.title: JSESSIONID cookie does not mean Jenkins
scenarios.description: Generic Java web application sets JSESSIONID cookie. JSESSIONID is a standard Java servlet container cookie, not Jenkins-specific.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: JSESSIONID is set by any Java servlet container (Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, etc.), not just Jenkins.

scenarios.title: sid cookie does not mean Kibana
scenarios.description: Generic dashboard sets sid cookie. sid is a common session ID cookie name used by many applications.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: The cookie name 'sid' is generic and used by many session management libraries.

scenarios.title: csrftoken cookie does not mean Django
scenarios.description: Node.js application sets csrftoken cookie. The cookie name alone does not identify Django.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: csrftoken is used by many CSRF protection libraries, not just Django.

scenarios.title: frontend cookie does not mean Magento
scenarios.description: Generic e-commerce store sets frontend cookie. The name 'frontend' is generic.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: The cookie name 'frontend' is generic and used by many applications for frontend session tracking.

scenarios.title: x-served-by: cache-xxx does not confirm Fastly
scenarios.description: Response has x-served-by: cache-lax17928-LAX header. Many CDNs and Varnish instances use this naming convention.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: The x-served-by: cache-xxx pattern is used by Varnish and multiple CDN providers, not exclusively Fastly.

scenarios.title: Apache-Coyote/1.1 is Tomcat, not Apache httpd
scenarios.description: Server header is Apache-Coyote/1.1 which identifies Tomcat's HTTP connector, not Apache HTTP Server.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Apache-Coyote is Tomcat's HTTP connector. CVE mapping must use Apache Tomcat, not Apache HTTP Server.

scenarios.title: ng-app without ng-version is not confirmed Angular
scenarios.description: Page has ng-app and ng-controller attributes but no ng-version. These are AngularJS 1.x directives that appear in legacy code and tutorials.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: ng-app and ng-controller are loose tokens from AngularJS 1.x. Without ng-version attribute, the Angular version cannot be confirmed.

scenarios.title: Generic JSON version field is not Nextcloud version
scenarios.description: API returns {version: '2.1.0'} but this is the inventory-api version, not Nextcloud.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A generic JSON 'version' field does not identify Nextcloud or its version. Only status.php with Nextcloud-specific keys should be used.

scenarios.title: Google Analytics measurement ID is not a software version
scenarios.description: Page contains G-ABC1234XYZ Google Analytics measurement ID. This is a tracking identifier, not a software version.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A GA measurement ID (G-xxx or UA-xxx) is a tracking identifier, not a software version number.

scenarios.title: Natural prose containing common words is not product detection
scenarios.description: Page contains words like 'server', 'admin', 'proxy' in natural text. Case-insensitive substring matching should not identify technologies.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Case-insensitive substring matching on single common words in page body produces false technology detections.

scenarios.title: Substring 'wp-content' in prose is not WordPress
scenarios.description: Page text says 'we wrap-content around the main container'. The substring 'wp-content' appears in 'wrap-content', but this is prose, not a WordPress path.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Substring matching of 'wp-content' within natural text like 'wrap-content' does not indicate WordPress.

scenarios.title: SPA catch-all returning same HTML for /admin is not an admin panel
scenarios.description: Single-page application returns identical HTML shell for every path including /admin, /login, /settings. The body is the same as the homepage.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A SPA catch-all returning HTTP 200 with the same HTML for /admin as for / is not evidence of an admin panel. The response must differ from the homepage and contain product-specific markers.

scenarios.title: Weak WordPress evidence without wp-json/generator/login
scenarios.description: Page mentions 'Powered by WordPress' in testimonial and has .wp-caption CSS class, but no wp-json API, no generator meta tag, no login form.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Weak evidence (text mention + CSS class) without structural confirmation (wp-json, generator meta, login form) is insufficient to confirm WordPress.

scenarios.title: Favicon hash comparison requires correct algorithm
scenarios.description: Custom favicon served. SHA-256 prefix must not be compared against MurmurHash3 fingerprint databases.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Shodan and similar databases use MurmurHash3 for favicon fingerprinting. SHA-256 prefixes are incompatible and will produce false matches.

scenarios.title: Generic sign-in page is not Grafana login
scenarios.description: Generic sign-in form with username/password fields. No Grafana-specific assets, cookies, or headers.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A password field and the word 'Sign in' on a /login URL is universal. Without Grafana-specific markers, this cannot be validated as Grafana.

scenarios.title: SPA catch-all is not a validated admin panel
scenarios.description: SPA returns identical HTML for /login as for /. HTTP 200 on a probed path is not validation.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: SPA catch-all routes return the same content for every path. A product-specific form field and unique content are required for validation.

scenarios.title: Prometheus probe URL returning homepage is not validation
scenarios.description: The /graph path returns the same homepage HTML. A docs site mentioning 'prometheus' at /graph is not Prometheus UI.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: The probe URL /graph returning the same content as the homepage does not validate Prometheus. Require Prometheus-specific UI strings.

scenarios.title: Generic 200 on /app/kibana is not Kibana
scenarios.description: Returns 200 with generic HTML at /app/kibana. No kbn-name header, no Kibana-specific bundle paths.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: HTTP 200 on a Kibana probe path without product-specific response content does not confirm Kibana.

scenarios.title: Sanctioned tools are not shadow IT
scenarios.description: Organization's approved tool inventory lists Grafana, Jenkins, GitLab. These are sanctioned and should not be flagged as shadow IT.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Tools that appear in the organization's known/approved asset inventory are sanctioned, not shadow IT. Only confirmed products outside the known inventory qualify.

scenarios.title: nginx 1.20.2 must not match CVEs for 1.2.x
scenarios.description: Server header reports nginx/1.20.2. String prefix '1.2' must not match version '1.20'. Numeric tuple comparison required.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Python startswith('1.2') incorrectly matches '1.20.2'. Version comparison must use numeric tuples: (1,20,2) > (1,2,9).

scenarios.title: Version string alone is not evidence of default configuration
scenarios.description: Server header nginx/1.24.0 does not mean the server has default/factory configuration.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A version string in a Server header indicates software identity, not configuration state. Only an unchanged setup wizard or known default credentials page indicates default configuration.

scenarios.title: Example Bearer tokens in documentation are not leaked secrets
scenarios.description: API documentation contains example curl commands with Bearer tokens and API keys. These are documentation fixtures.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Documentation examples containing placeholder tokens, test prefixes (sk_test_), and explicit markers (example_only, do_not_use) are not leaked secrets.

scenarios.title: Private IPs in educational article are not operational leakage
scenarios.description: Blog post about private networking mentions 192.168.1.1, 10.0.0.5 in educational context.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: RFC1918 addresses in article prose about networking are educational content, not operational leakage. Only addresses in headers, script assignments, redirects, or error responses constitute leakage.

scenarios.title: 'Index of' in article title is not a directory listing
scenarios.description: Article titled 'Index of Best Practices for Apache Security'. The phrase 'Index of' appears in editorial content.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: The phrase 'Index of' in article text, blog titles, or editorial content is not a directory listing. Require <title>Index of /path</title> plus Parent Directory links.

scenarios.title: Standard Server/X-Powered-By headers are not internal secrets
scenarios.description: Response includes Server: nginx/1.25.3 and X-Powered-By: Express. These are standard runtime identification headers.
incorrect_findings: Internal secrets leaking via Server header
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Generic Server and X-Powered-By values are fingerprinting data, not internal secrets. Versioned banners with known CVEs are a separate concern from 'secret leakage'.

scenarios.title: Missing security headers should be grouped as one finding
scenarios.description: Page is missing CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. These should be reported as ONE grouped hardening finding, not 6 separate findings.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Ten separate findings for missing headers floods the report. Group them. X-XSS-Protection is obsolete and should not be required.

scenarios.title: Analytics cookies without Secure/HttpOnly are not a security finding
scenarios.description: Page sets _ga and _gid cookies without Secure/HttpOnly flags. These are analytics cookies that do not contain sensitive session data.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Only session identifiers missing Secure or HttpOnly on HTTPS should generate findings. Analytics cookies (_ga, _gid), consent cookies, and locale preferences do not need these flags.

scenarios.title: x-amz-cf-id header is CloudFront, not a public S3 bucket
scenarios.description: Response includes x-amz-cf-id header. This is a CloudFront distribution request ID, not evidence of a publicly accessible S3 bucket.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: x-amz-cf-id is a CloudFront CDN header present on any AWS-fronted website. It indicates CDN delivery, not bucket access. Require ListBucket XML or x-amz-bucket-region on an object-storage endpoint.

scenarios.title: Standard libraries are not malicious dependencies
scenarios.description: Page loads React, jQuery, Bootstrap from CDNs. These are standard first-party framework dependencies.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: The application's own framework (React, Vue, Angular) and standard libraries (jQuery, Bootstrap) loaded from major CDNs are not malicious dependencies.

scenarios.title: HTTP 200 on /manage is not access control weakness
scenarios.description: Public page 'Manage Your Subscription' returns 200. The word 'manage' in the URL and page title is not evidence of an unprotected admin endpoint.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: HTTP 200 plus a technology name containing 'manage' does not indicate access control weakness. Require actual sensitive data returned without authentication.

scenarios.title: Missing CORS headers is the safe default
scenarios.description: JSON API endpoint with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Missing CORS means the browser enforces same-origin policy, which is the safe default.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Missing CORS headers means the browser's same-origin policy applies. This is the secure default. Only report CORS issues when Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.

scenarios.title: Unreachable HTTPS is not a certificate failure
scenarios.description: HTTPS connection to port 3015 is refused/unreachable. This is a connectivity issue, not a certificate error.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Connection refused or timeout on HTTPS is a reachability issue, not a certificate problem. Only report certificate issues when the TLS handshake returns an actual certificate error (expired, hostname mismatch, untrusted chain).

scenarios.title: Same HTTP fact must not be reported twice
scenarios.description: If HTTP and HTTPS both serve content, this should produce one finding about cleartext HTTP, not separate findings for 'HTTP and HTTPS both serve content' and 'Content served over HTTP'.
incorrect_findings: HTTP and HTTPS both serve content AND Content served over HTTP (duplicate)
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Two findings describing the same observation (cleartext HTTP serving content) wastes reviewer time. Keep one finding.

scenarios.title: HTTP 403 is not 'content served over HTTP'
scenarios.description: HTTP listener returns 403 Forbidden. A 403 response is the hardened state and should not be reported as content being served.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A 403 on port 80 is often the hardened state. Only report when HTTP serves actual 2xx content.

scenarios.title: Unknown version must not map to KEV CVEs
scenarios.description: Technology entry with version: null and confidence: 'assumed'. KEV-flagged CVEs should not be attached to technologies with no confirmed version.
incorrect_findings: CVE-2021-43798 (Grafana KEV) applied to unknown version
CVE-2024-23897 (Jenkins KEV) applied to unknown version
scenarios.fp_reasoning: A technology with no version and heuristic evidence should not inherit Known Exploited Vulnerability entries. Map CVEs only from confirmed versions or behavioral probes.

scenarios.title: Open-ended NVD version ranges must be handled carefully
scenarios.description: CVEs with no upper bound in their affected version range (e.g., >= 0 with no end) should not automatically match all versions.
scenarios.fp_reasoning: Open-ended NVD ranges (lower bound set, no upper bound) require careful evaluation. A CVE from 2009 with no upper bound should not auto-match current software versions.

scenarios.title: Failed behavioral probe must gate CVE attachment
scenarios.description: Grafana /api/health returns 401 (not authenticated). The behavioral probe fails, so CVEs for Grafana should not be attached.
incorrect_findings: Grafana CVEs attached without probe validation
scenarios.fp_reasoning: When a behavioral probe (Jenkins crumb, Grafana /api/health, CouchDB server response) fails, CVE mapping must be rejected for that product.

scenarios.title: Assumed/heuristic versions must not auto-file CVEs
scenarios.description: Technology with version_source: 'heuristic' and confidence: 'assumed' must not automatically generate CVE findings.
incorrect_findings: CVE applied based on assumed version
scenarios.fp_reasoning: An assumed version from a heuristic source (e.g., body filename pattern) is not confirmed. It should not drive CVE attachment unless corroborated by a header or Nuclei extractor.

scenarios.title: Real Grafana must be correctly identified
scenarios.description: Real Grafana OSS instance with grafana_session cookie, x-grafana-version header, /api/health endpoint.

scenarios.title: Real Jenkins must be correctly identified
scenarios.description: Real Jenkins instance with X-Jenkins header, crumb endpoint, jenkins_remember_me cookie.

scenarios.title: Strong Grafana fingerprint via mock must be detected
scenarios.description: Mock service returning x-grafana-version: 10.2.0 header and valid /api/health response.

scenarios.title: Strong Jenkins fingerprint via mock must be detected
scenarios.description: Mock service returning X-Jenkins: 2.426.3 header.

scenarios.title: Strong Kibana fingerprint must be detected
scenarios.description: kbn-name: kibana and kbn-version: 8.11.1 headers present.

scenarios.title: Strong WordPress fingerprint must be detected
scenarios.description: Generator meta tag, wp-json API, wp-content paths, and login form present.

scenarios.title: Real Nextcloud status.php must be detected
scenarios.description: Nextcloud-specific status.php response with productname and oc_ cookie.

scenarios.title: ng-version attribute must be detected as Angular
scenarios.description: app-root element with ng-version='17.0.0' attribute.

scenarios.title: SQL Injection in findings sort parameter
scenarios.description: The sort query parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL ORDER BY clause without parameterization.

scenarios.title: IDOR on user profile endpoint
scenarios.description: GET /api/users/:id returns any user's profile without org_id check, allowing cross-tenant data access.

scenarios.title: IDOR on asset detail endpoint
scenarios.description: GET /api/assets/:id returns any asset without org_id check.

scenarios.title: Stored XSS in finding comments
scenarios.description: Finding comments are stored without sanitization and rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML in the frontend.

scenarios.title: SSRF via asset import URL
scenarios.description: POST /api/assets/import accepts a URL parameter and fetches it server-side without validation.

scenarios.title: Privilege escalation via mass assignment
scenarios.description: PATCH /api/users/:id accepts role field, allowing a viewer to promote themselves to admin.

scenarios.title: SQL injection via debug parameter on admin stats
scenarios.description: GET /api/admin/stats?sql= passes raw SQL to the database for execution.

scenarios.title: Weak JWT secret
scenarios.description: JWT secret is a dictionary word (soltrisk-secret-key-2024) that can be brute-forced.

scenarios.title: Rate limit bypass via X-Forwarded-For
scenarios.description: Rate limiter uses X-Forwarded-For header for client identification, allowing bypass by spoofing the header.

scenarios.title: Open registration to any organization
scenarios.description: POST /api/auth/register accepts org_id parameter, allowing registration into any organization.

scenarios.title: Credentials leaked in HTML comment
scenarios.description: index.html contains an HTML comment with development credentials: admin@soltrisk.local / Admin123!

scenarios.title: Server environment variables exposed
scenarios.description: GET /debug/env returns process.env as JSON, exposing server configuration and secrets.

scenarios.title: Internal IP leaked in error response
scenarios.description: Error response reveals internal database address 10.42.0.15:5432 in the error details.

scenarios.title: Directory listing with sensitive files
scenarios.description: Directory listing exposes backup.sql.gz and config.old files.

scenarios.title: Debug token leaked in response header
scenarios.description: X-Debug-Token header exposes internal debug session information.

scenarios.title: CORS wildcard with credentials enabled
scenarios.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.

scenarios.title: Session cookie without Secure/HttpOnly flags
scenarios.description: The weak_session cookie is a session identifier without Secure or HttpOnly flags.

scenarios.title: Public S3-style bucket listing with sensitive files
scenarios.description: Bucket listing XML exposes backup.sql and credentials.env files.

scenarios.title: Prometheus metrics endpoint publicly accessible
scenarios.description: The /metrics endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication, exposing internal service metrics.

scenarios.title: Deprecated nginx 1.2.9 detected
scenarios.description: Server header reveals nginx/1.2.9 which is end-of-life and has known CVEs.
